decision: Do not adopt blanket neural-world freezing or expand formal control experiments yet.
evidence_scope: Completed native preflight and four real controls, seeds6201/6202 crossed with stable/local_speed_drop; same initialization, target duration and global-label/policy-update budget as action_model.
observations: Frozen world improves stable full-day costs in both seeds, but worsens shock full-day and post-stop costs in both seeds.
Frozen world has lower average global prediction error on its own trajectories, but lower trust; these metrics do not rank control performance consistently.
Prediction scores are on different realized trajectories, not matched factual transitions, and trust measures postfit six-head Bellman confidence rather than raw prequential global MSE.
next_step: A new v6 passive diagnosis on the existing action_model development setup: retain the initial frozen world twin in server memory; score both worlds at the same causal issues and on the next untrained selected packet, separately per family and under the same selected family; record six-head error, common-evaluator Bellman error, trust training error/tau/instantaneous confidence/bootstrap and actor-action weights. Any twin trust learner must receive the same observed replay sequence, rather than remaining at its initial state.
optimizer_followup: Extend matched eight-step shadows to online versus frozen neural worlds, using shared replay/target draws and fixed actual trust, to isolate how parameter adaptation changes the critic, action preferences and next-packet TD. No shadow branch controls the environment.
gates: Require exact reproduction of baseline control cost and unchanged label/update budgets. A model-update revision is justified only after same-flow held-future and action-value evidence identify a specific failure; then test a small stable/shock control comparison before any formal expansion.
